exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift

source_english.description: A sumo deadlift lifts a barbell from a wide toes-out stance by extending the hips and knees together.
instructions: Stand over the bar with feet wide and toes turned outward, then grip it inside the knees.
Brace the trunk and push the floor away while keeping the chest lifted.
Extend the hips and knees until standing tall with the bar close to the body.
Lower the bar by bending the hips and knees while maintaining the wide stance.
form_cues: Keep the bar close to the legs.
Hinge from the hips with a long spine.
Drive the floor away to stand.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees into a squat.
Jerking the bar from the floor.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load and range that preserve a neutral back throughout the hinge.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat (Barbell)

source_english.description: Sumo Squat (Barbell) lowers the hips by bending the hips and knees and returns to standing by driving through the feet.
instructions: Place the barbell across the upper back and stand with feet wider than shoulder width, toes turned outward.
Brace the trunk and lower by bending the hips and knees, keeping the knees aligned with the toes.
Descend until the thighs approach parallel or the deepest controlled position.
Drive through both feet to extend the hips and knees and stand tall.
form_cues: Keep the knees tracking the toes.
Brace the trunk through the depth.
common_mistakes: Bouncing or cutting the depth short.
source_english.safety_note: Use a rack or machine stops and choose a depth you can control with both feet planted.

exercises.name: Upright Row (Barbell)

source_english.description: Upright Row (Barbell) pulls a barbell from the thighs toward the upper chest with the elbows leading.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell with an overhand grip at the thighs.
Brace the abdomen and pull the elbows upward and outward, keeping the load close to the body.
Stop when the hands reach the upper chest or before the shoulders pinch.
Lower the resistance slowly to the thighs and reset.
common_mistakes: Pulling above a comfortable shoulder range.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop below any painful shoulder height.

Bend the elbows outward to lower the dumbbells toward the shoulders.

exercises.name: Band Pullaparts

source_english.description: Band Pullaparts keep the arms near shoulder height while the resistance band is stretched apart by the upper back.
instructions: Stand or sit tall holding the resistance band at shoulder height with arms straight.
Pull your hands apart by squeezing between the shoulder blades.
Pause when the band reaches the chest line without flaring the ribs.
Return slowly until the band is lightly tensioned.

source_english.safety_note: Use a light band so it cannot snap back toward the hands.

exercises.name: Chest Dip

source_english.description: The Chest Dip lowers the body by bending the elbows between parallel supports, then presses back up while the shoulders remain controlled.
instructions: Mount the parallel handles with arms straight and the torso slightly inclined.

Pause before the shoulders lose control.
Press through the handles to straighten the elbows and reset.
source_english.safety_note: Use the assistance platform or a lighter load if the full dip depth cannot stay controlled.
